notes: Main kinds of disagreement: (1) document stance: coder A coded delegates for the Provost, Guarini and Thayer policies, coder B restrict; resolved to restrict because each states its own ban-unless-permitted rule ('may not use ... unless expressly permitted', 'only if permitted by their program, advisor, or course instructor') even though permission is delegated; DCAL agreed (delegates). (2) actor and phase on rationale/principle statements inside syllabus examples and in the Guarini/Thayer data-protection explanation (A all/general, B student/during-work): resolved to student with phase general, since the statement is addressed to students but governs no work step; P63 faculty-support units were resolved to actor instructor. (3) modality on example sentences in the DCAL case studies (informs vs may/must-not/must): resolved by the wording ('was unacceptable' must-not, 'could choose' and 'was allowed' may, 'asked students to engage' must, 'should' kept as should). (4) policy_type: P19 vs P23 for 'copy and paste material generated by AI' (resolved to P23, which names never copy-paste), P36 vs P28 for 'without proper attribution violates academic integrity' (P28), P05 vs P35 for stage-by-stage guardrails (P35, no named tiers), P24 vs P44 for Boke's 'working directly with AI writing tools' (P44), P04 vs P09 and P11 vs P04 for the Provost sentences, P36 vs P10 for 'failure to clarify is not a justification' (P36), P17 vs P25 for the DartmouthChat sample (P25). (5) unit_stance: mostly A require vs B permit on disclosure duties; resolved to require for must/should duties and neutral for rationale, consequences and samples. (6) single-coder units: B found 16 extra units (Approved-use lists, Regis/Joubin duties, rationale sentences, the acknowledgement-method sentence in the Provost policy), all real and kept; A-only units were 6 kept (sample citation, DartmouthChat sample recoded P25, CS-course literacy rationale, 'they evolve and change', Guarini/Thayer 'considerations' sentence) and 2 dropped (the grant caption and the 'inferior free models' remark, which state no rule). Matching: Guarini/Thayer aligned unit by unit; two DCAL pairs (art history, Socratic questioner) and the Provost ask-first sentences were merged by hand because the coders anchored different parts of one passage. new_types empty on both sides.
